stories.headline: US negotiates long-term lease of 17 Venezuelan oil fields as Caracas weighs leaving OPEC

key_facts.fact: Trump administration officials are working on a deal to secure long-term US access to part of Venezuela's crude reserves, sources said on Thursday, August 27; the agreement could be signed and made public soon.
key_facts.excerpt: HOUSTON/WASHINGTON, Aug 27 (Reuters) - Trump administration officials are working on a deal to secure long-term access to a portion of Venezuela's crude reserves, sources with knowledge of the negotiations said on Thursday, a move that could ultimately lower the cost of oil imports.

key_facts.fact: A list of 17 fields under negotiation seen by Reuters includes green fields in the Orinoco Belt plus mature areas in Lake Maracaibo, some currently operated by a small Chinese firm under a contract signed during Maduro's government.
key_facts.excerpt: A list of 17 fields in negotiation seen by Reuters includes green fields in the vast Orinoco Belt combined with mature areas in Lake Maracaibo, some of which are currently operated by a small Chinese firm whose contract was signed during Maduro's administration.

key_facts.fact: A 'lease' is under consideration as the legal model, with a further auction or tender to allocate each field among US producers; the resulting supply would be guaranteed for the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate source said a "lease" was in consideration as the legal model to make the deal work, with a further auction or tender to allocate each one of the fields among U.S. producers.

key_facts.fact: Venezuela is considering leaving OPEC as it strengthens ties with the US, Bloomberg reported late on Thursday; Venezuela was a founding member of the group in 1960 and now produces about 1.25 million barrels per day.
key_facts.excerpt: Venezuela is considering leaving the OPEC oil production group as it strengthens ties with the U.S., Bloomberg reported late on Thursday. Venezuela, which joined the group as a founding member in 1960, has not met OPEC quotas for years.

key_facts.fact: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright is planning a trip to Caracas as soon as next week, according to Axios, which first reported the talks on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: Axios first reported on the talks on Thursday and said U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright is planning a trip to Caracas as soon as next week.

key_facts.fact: The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve holds about 290 million barrels, roughly 41% of capacity, after draws following the 2022 Russian invasion and the start of the Iran war in February 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The SPR currently holds about 290 million barrels in underground salt caverns, about 41% of its total capacity.

key_facts.fact: Oil settled up about 2% on August 27: October WTI closed up $1.30 (1.6%) at $83.53 a barrel and October Brent was up $1.94 (2.2%) at $89.78.
key_facts.excerpt: Aug. 27 | October WTI Crude Oil Contract Closes Up $1.30, or 1.6%; Settles at $83.53 per Barrel. October Brent Oil Last seen up $1.94, or 2.2%, to $89.78.

sources.title: US nears deal to secure long-term access to Venezuela's oil reserves, sources say

stories.headline: Advent and Stripe abandon their $53bn buyout of PayPal, and the stock drops 13%

key_facts.fact: A consortium of buyout firm Advent International and payment processor Stripe decided to abandon its pursuit of PayPal, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, August 27.
key_facts.excerpt: Aug 27 (Reuters) - A consortium of buyout firm Advent and payment processor Stripe has decided to abandon its pursuit of fintech pioneer PayPal, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The group had bid $60.50 per share in July, valuing PayPal at more than $53 billion — a fraction of the roughly $360 billion the company was worth at its 2021 pandemic peak.
key_facts.excerpt: The payments company, once the crown jewel of American financial technology, received a $60.50-per-share bid from Stripe and private equity firm Advent International, which valued it at more than $53 billion, Reuters reported in July... a fraction of the roughly $360 billion valuation PayPal commanded as a pandemic-era darling in 2021.

key_facts.fact: PayPal's board considered the offer inadequate and said it faced regulatory and financing hurdles; the company never formally responded to the proposal.
key_facts.excerpt: PayPal's board saw the takeover bid as inadequate and said it faced regulatory and financing hurdles, Reuters had previously reported. PayPal has not formally responded to the proposal.

key_facts.fact: PayPal shares slumped 13% in premarket trading on Friday, August 28, last trading at $53.20 after closing at $61.47 the previous session.
key_facts.excerpt: PayPal shares slumped 13% in premarket trading on Friday, after Bloomberg News reported that a consortium of buyout firm Advent and payment processor Stripe had abandoned its pursuit of the fintech pioneer... last trading at $53.20 before the bell, [after] closing at $61.47.

key_facts.fact: The deal would have ranked among the largest leveraged buyouts ever; Block had first approached PayPal alongside Stripe and Advent in April but left the consortium before the offer was submitted.
key_facts.excerpt: A consortium of buyout firm Advent and payment processor Stripe has decided to abandon its pursuit of fintech pioneer PayPal Holdings, a potential deal that would have ranked as one of the biggest ever leveraged buyouts.

key_facts.fact: PayPal's new CEO Enrique Lores has said the company would carefully consider any strategic option it believes could create superior shareholder value.
key_facts.excerpt: In the company's most recent earnings call, Lores did not comment on the takeover speculation but said PayPal would carefully consider any opportunity or strategic option that it believes could create superior value for shareholders.

stories.headline: Qatar's PM flies to Tehran to revive Hormuz talks as Trump says the US will not speak to Iran

key_facts.fact: Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani visited Tehran on Thursday, August 27, meeting Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Qatar's Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani on Thursday discussed a proposed framework... Sheikh Mohammed, who is both prime minister and foreign minister of Qatar, later met separately with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliament speaker and top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

key_facts.fact: The framework under discussion includes a temporary joint Iranian-Omani shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and a joint project to clear the waterway of mines Iran says were laid during the war.
key_facts.excerpt: [They] discussed a proposed framework that includes the creation of a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a possible 'joint project' to clear the strait of mines, the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement. Iran says the mines were laid during the war.

key_facts.fact: Trump said in the Oval Office that Washington is not talking to Iran: 'We don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office after the White House said a US economic campaign against Tehran would continue until Iran decides to negotiate meaningfully.

key_facts.fact: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt described the shift on Thursday: 'We've had Operation Epic Fury to destroy their military. Now we have Operation Economic Outcast to destroy their economy.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We've had Operation Epic Fury to destroy their military. Now we have Operation Economic Outcast to destroy their economy," Leavitt said in an interview with Fox News.

key_facts.fact: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told the Qatari PM that Tehran would strike US military and economic interests if Washington engaged in 'mischief', and that the US must end its port blockade, pay compensation and lift sanctions before the strait reopens.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told the Qatari prime minister that Tehran would strike US military and economic interests if Washington engaged in "mischief" against Iran... Those conditions include an end to the US blockade on Iranian ports, compensation and removal of sanctions.

key_facts.fact: The International Maritime Organization has recorded 70 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began on February 28, killing 19 seafarers; about a fifth of global energy supplies passed through the strait before the war.
key_facts.excerpt: The International Maritime Organization has reported 70 incidents in the strait since Feb 28 that have killed 19 seafarers.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC Navy likely attacked a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on August 27, and Basij commander Hossein Taeb warned the same day that Iran would impose economic costs on the US and Israel.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC Navy separately likely attacked a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on August 27... Basij Commander Hossein Taeb warned on August 27 that Iran will respond to US economic pressure by imposing economic costs on the United States and Israel.

stories.headline: FDA clears first oral dermatomyositis drug and Gilead's smallest single-tablet HIV regimen same day

key_facts.fact: On August 27 the FDA approved LISRAYA (brepocitinib) 30 mg, a once-daily pill from Roivant's subsidiary Priovant, for adults with dermatomyositis — the first major therapeutic advance in decades for the autoimmune disease. It is available in the US immediately.
key_facts.excerpt: BASEL, Switzerland and LONDON and NEW YORK, Aug. 27, 2026 -- Roivant (Nasdaq: ROIV) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved LISRAYA (brepocitinib) 30 mg for the treatment of adults with dermatomyositis (DM). LISRAYA is a pill taken once daily.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 VALOR trial — the largest dermatomyositis study ever run — 55% of patients on LISRAYA achieved both moderate-or-better improvement on the myositis Total Improvement Score and minimal or no steroid use by week 52, versus 30% on placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: Most patients treated with LISRAYA were able to achieve both moderate or better improvement on the Total Improvement Score and minimal or no steroid use by the end of the study (55%, compared to 30% on placebo).

key_facts.fact: Among patients on at least 7.5 mg/day of oral corticosteroids at baseline, 62% tapered to minimal or no steroid use versus 38% on placebo, and 45% came off corticosteroids entirely versus 29%.
key_facts.excerpt: Among patients receiving LISRAYA who were taking >=7.5 mg/day (prednisone-equivalent) of oral corticosteroids at baseline, 62% tapered to minimal or no steroid use (<=2.5 mg/day) by the end of the 52-week study, compared with 38% on placebo; 45% came off corticosteroids entirely, compared with 29% on placebo.

key_facts.fact: The FDA's 2026 novel drug approvals list records Lisraya (brepocitinib) as approval number 35 of the year, dated 8/27/2026, to treat dermatomyositis in adults.
key_facts.excerpt: | 35. | Lisraya | brepocitinib | 8/27/2026 | To treat dermatomyositis in adults |

key_facts.fact: Also on August 27, the FDA approved Gilead's Bixlenvo (bictegravir 75 mg / lenacapavir 50 mg), the smallest once-daily single-tablet regimen for HIV and the first such option for virologically suppressed patients on complex multi-drug regimens.
key_facts.excerpt: Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Bixlenvo (bictegravir 75 mg/lenacapavir 50 mg), the smallest once-daily single tablet regimen (STR) for the treatment of HIV in adults who are virologically suppressed.

key_facts.fact: Bixlenvo's approval rests on the Phase 3 ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2 trials; ARTISTRY-1 enrolled the oldest population in an HIV registrational trial to date, median age 60, with participants taking between two and 11 pills a day at baseline and a median 28 years of prior treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: ARTISTRY-1 enrolled the oldest study population in a Phase 3 registrational trial for HIV-1 treatment to date, with a median participant age of 60 years. Participants were taking between two and 11 pills per day at baseline... with a median treatment duration of 28 years.

sources.title: Roivant Announces FDA Approval of LISRAYA (brepocitinib) for Adults with Dermatomyositis; Now Available in the U.S.

stories.headline: US jobless claims fall to 203,000, near a 60-year low, in a 'no hire, no fire' labor market

key_facts.fact: Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 4,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 for the week ended August 22, the Labor Department reported on Thursday, August 27; economists polled by Reuters had forecast 208,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 4,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 for the week ended August 22, the Labor Department said on Thursday (Aug 27). Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 208,000 claims for the latest week.

key_facts.fact: The four-week moving average ticked up to 205,500, while continuing claims — a proxy for hiring — fell 18,000 to 1.778 million in the week ended August 15.
key_facts.excerpt: Jobless claims slipped to 203,000 last week from a revised 207,000 the week before, the Labor Department reported Thursday. The four-week average of claims, which smooths out week-to-week ups and downs, ticked up slightly to 205,500.

key_facts.fact: Claims are hovering at the low end of this year's 189,000-230,000 range, indicating layoffs remain rare even as hiring is soft; the US unemployment rate is 4.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Claims are hovering in the lower end of their 189,000-230,000 range for this year, indicating that layoffs remain low even if hiring is soft. The US jobless rate ticked down again last month to 4.1 per cent, a historically low level.

key_facts.fact: Labor-market stability, if sustained, lets the Federal Reserve keep focusing on inflation, which has run above its 2% target for 65 straight months.
key_facts.excerpt: Labour market stability if sustained could allow the Federal Reserve to keep its focus on containing inflation that has run above its 2 per cent target for 65 straight months.

key_facts.fact: AP notes the job market has stayed resilient despite high gasoline prices caused by the fighting with Iran, partly because Trump's immigration crackdown and baby-boomer retirements mean fewer people competing for jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. economy and job market have proved resilient in the face of high gasoline prices caused by the fighting with Iran. The U.S. unemployment rate is low at 4.1%. That is partly because President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown and the ongoing retirement of baby boomers mean that fewer people are competing for jobs.

stories.headline: Russia calls its overnight barrage on nine Ukrainian cities 'massive'; strikes ran into Thursday

key_facts.fact: Russia's overnight barrage of missiles and jet-powered drones struck nine Ukrainian cities, damaging homes, schools, medical facilities and ports, killing at least two people and injuring more than a dozen.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's 'massive' overnight barrage of missiles and jet-powered drones hammered nine Ukrainian cities, damaging homes, schools, medical facilities and ports, killing at least two people and injuring more than a dozen.

key_facts.fact: The onslaught ran into the daylight hours of Thursday, August 27, with explosions echoing around Kyiv through the morning.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia bombarded cities across Ukraine with missiles and drones in an overnight onslaught that ran into the daylight of hours Thursday, when explosions echoed around Kyiv through the morning.

key_facts.fact: Shortages of US-made Patriot air defenses leave Ukraine exposed as Russia rebuilds missile stockpiles and targets energy and private businesses to cripple the economy before winter.
key_facts.excerpt: Shortages of Patriot air defenses leave Ukraine vulnerable as Russia repeatedly builds missile stockpiles, targets energy and private businesses, and seeks to cripple the economy ahead of winter.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine is escalating its own long-range drone campaign against Russian command posts and major online retailers, while stray drones over neighboring Moldova fuel fears the war could spill across borders.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine escalates its own long-range drone campaign, hitting Russian command posts and major online retailers, while stray drones over neighboring Moldova underscore fears the war could spill across borders.

stories.headline: Farm groups urge Trump to drop a refinery-waiver expansion meant to cut gasoline prices

key_facts.fact: A coalition of farm and biofuel groups — including the Renewable Fuels Association, Growth Energy and the National Farmers Union — wrote to Trump on Thursday, August 27, urging him to reject any expansion of small-refinery exemptions from US biofuel blending laws.
key_facts.excerpt: A coalition of farm and biofuel groups urged Trump on Thursday to reject any waiver expansion, warning that a surge in exemptions for small refineries would hurt rural America by undercutting demand for crops and renewable fuels.

key_facts.fact: The administration is considering roughly doubling the exemptions, from 990 million credits to as many as 1.8 billion, with a decision expected before the end of August.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration is considering roughly doubling the size of the exemptions, from 990 million credits to as many as 1.8 billion, sources have told Reuters. A decision is expected before the end of August.

key_facts.fact: Trump and top officials discussed a plan to raise 2027 biofuel quotas by about 500 million gallons to offset the damage from the coming exemptions, two people familiar with the meeting said; no final decision has been made.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration is considering a plan that would increase biofuel quotas for the 2027 calendar year by roughly 500 million gallons to offset any damage caused by the soon-to-be-announced exemptions for smaller refineries, two separate sources told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The move is aimed at taming gasoline prices during the war with Iran ahead of November midterm elections; the prospect of the waivers already sent prices for renewable fuel credits (RINs) sharply lower.
key_facts.excerpt: They said the administration wants to tame surging gasoline prices to help Trump's fellow Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm elections. The prospect of a large expansion of refinery waivers had traders anticipating weaker demand for biofuels, sending prices for renewable fuel credits, known as RINs, sharply lower.

key_facts.fact: Iowa Republican senator Joni Ernst called the plan 'a handout to Big Oil falsely marketed as relief at the pump,' saying it would crush demand for corn and soybeans.
key_facts.excerpt: Senator Joni Ernst, a Republican from Iowa, has criticized the potential expansion of the exemptions, telling Reuters in a statement that it is "a handout to Big Oil falsely marketed as relief at the pump."

sources.title: US officials weigh plan to shield farmers from expansion of refinery biofuel waivers, sources say
